title: NodeHold
description: A node's external wait (docs/design/m0/02 "Hold reasons and resume signals"; 13): approvals, quotas, human acts, probes. Internal inputs wait structurally and need no hold (13). A replacement node keeps a transferred hold's id, signal instance, owner and paging history, so escalation never restarts (13 supersession). It records the owner, escalation and page_after in force when it was raised, so a later registry edit changes no recorded hold. Lease holds stay on the lease (05). owner_ref is set exactly for the owner kinds that name a concrete owner: the grant holder's actor id, the named owner, or the environment owner the profile names. A conditional admits only plain keywords (internal/schemagen), so the schema checks the actor id's act_ TypeID shape by pattern and internal/graph checks its UUIDv7 bits (adc-typeid).

hold.description: A registered hold (schemas/vocab/holds.yaml); internal/graph checks that it is registered.

reason.description: The reason of the result that raised it, whose registry entry names this hold (02; 12, e.g. evidence_cap_exhausted with wrong_owner). Null for a hold the resolver raised with no result, e.g. awaiting_input for a declared answer.

signal_instance.description: The concrete signal that resumes it, e.g. the reset time or the approval id awaited (02).

owner.description: Who owns the hold now: the owner it was raised with, or its escalate_to once paged after page_after.

escalate_to.description: Who owns the hold once page_after passes, as in force when it was raised: the registry's escalate_to or, for an environment owner the profile does not name, the operator (02); null keeps the owner.

escalate_ref.description: The concrete escalation owner, by the owner_ref rule; null when escalate_to is null or names none.

page_after.description: The page_after in force when it was raised (02; a project may override the registry's). Null: the hold is never paged.

since.description: When the wait began; page_after counts from here, also across a transfer.

pages.description: The paging history, oldest first and append-only: who was paged, by the same owner_ref rule. Pages are deduplicated by hold id and signal instance, never by channel (02).

channel.description: Where the owner was paged, when the pager reports it; null otherwise.
